summary: Disulfiram is an oral alcohol-deterrent used as an aid in selected, motivated chronic alcohol patients who want enforced sobriety while receiving supportive and psychotherapeutic treatment. By inhibiting aldehyde dehydrogenase, it makes any alcohol intake produce a highly unpleasant disulfiram-alcohol reaction. It must never be given to an intoxicated patient or without the patient's full knowledge, and is contraindicated with alcohol-containing products, metronidazole, severe myocardial disease, coronary occlusion, and psychoses. Severe and sometimes fatal hepatitis can occur.
indications: Aid in the management of selected chronic alcohol patients who want to remain in enforced sobriety, as an adjunct to supportive and psychotherapeutic treatment (not a cure for alcoholism)

dosage.d: Maximum 500 mg once daily as a single dose
dosage.n: Never start until abstinent from alcohol for at least 12 hours; take in morning, or at bedtime if sedative effect

dosage.d: Average 250 mg daily (range 125 to 500 mg); do not exceed 500 mg/day
dosage.t: Months to years until socially recovered
dosage.n: Continue daily uninterrupted; may crush and mix with liquid to confirm adherence

admin: NEVER administer to a patient in a state of alcohol intoxication
NEVER administer without the patient's full knowledge
Do not start until the patient has abstained from alcohol for at least 12 hours
Fully inform the patient of the disulfiram-alcohol reaction and caution against surreptitious drinking
Tablets may be crushed and well mixed with liquid
Instruct relatives accordingly; supervised alcohol-challenge tests are largely abandoned and never in patients over 50
moa: Disulfiram blocks the oxidation of alcohol at the acetaldehyde stage by inhibiting aldehyde dehydrogenase. When alcohol is then ingested, blood acetaldehyde rises to 5-10 times normal, producing the disulfiram-alcohol reaction. The reaction is proportional to the dose of both drug and alcohol and persists as long as alcohol is being metabolized; tolerance does not develop and sensitivity increases with prolonged therapy.

absolute: Patients in a state of alcohol intoxication or given the drug without their full knowledge
Receiving or recently received alcohol or alcohol-containing preparations (cough syrups, tonics, etc.)
Receiving or recently received metronidazole or paraldehyde
Severe myocardial disease or coronary occlusion
Hypersensitivity to disulfiram or other thiuram derivatives (used in pesticides/rubber)

preg: Safe use in pregnancy has not been established. Disulfiram should be used during pregnancy only when, in the physician's judgment, the probable benefits outweigh the possible risks.
lact: It is not known whether disulfiram is excreted in human milk. Because many drugs are excreted in milk, disulfiram should not be given to nursing mothers.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is provided, but because of the risk of an accidental disulfiram-alcohol reaction, use with extreme caution in patients with acute or chronic nephritis.
hepatic: Severe and sometimes fatal hepatitis, including hepatic failure requiring transplantation or death, may occur even after months of therapy and in patients with or without prior abnormal liver function. Use with extreme caution in hepatic cirrhosis or insufficiency; obtain baseline and follow-up (10-14 day) liver function tests and advise patients to report fatigue, weakness, malaise, anorexia, nausea, vomiting, jaundice, or dark urine.

major: Phenytoin and congeners - disulfiram slows metabolism, risking phenytoin intoxication; obtain baseline level and monitor
Metronidazole - contraindicated; risk of combined toxicity and psychotic reactions
Paraldehyde - contraindicated; structurally related to acetaldehyde
Oral anticoagulants - disulfiram may prolong prothrombin time; adjust dose on starting/stopping
Isoniazid - watch for unsteady gait or marked mental status changes; discontinue disulfiram if they appear
moderate: Barbiturates - administered concurrently without untoward effects, but consider risk of new abuse
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; avoid foods containing alcohol (sauces, vinegars)
interactions.alcohol: Avoid ALL alcohol in every form - beverages, sauces, vinegars, cough mixtures, tonics, aftershave lotions and back rubs - during therapy and for up to 14 days after the last dose; even small amounts can trigger the disulfiram-alcohol reaction
interactions.diagnostics: Avoid exposure to ethylene dibromide or its vapors (animal data suggest a toxic interaction)

common: Skin eruptions / acneform eruptions / allergic dermatitis
serious: Hepatitis (cholestatic or fulminant) and hepatic failure - may be fatal or require transplantation
Optic neuritis, peripheral neuritis, polyneuritis, peripheral neuropathy
emergency: Severe disulfiram-alcohol reaction: respiratory depression, cardiovascular collapse, arrhythmias, myocardial infarction, acute congestive heart failure, unconsciousness, convulsions, death

monitoring: Baseline and follow-up (10-14 day) liver function tests
Complete blood count and serum chemistries including LFTs
Early symptoms of hepatitis (fatigue, anorexia, nausea, jaundice, dark urine)
Prothrombin time when on oral anticoagulants
Adherence (consider crushing and mixing with liquid)
counsel: Avoid ALL alcohol in every disguised form (sauces, vinegars, cough mixtures, aftershave, back rubs); reactions can occur up to 14 days after stopping
Understand that even small amounts of alcohol cause flushing, throbbing headache, nausea, vomiting, palpitations and can be life-threatening
Take exactly as prescribed; never take while intoxicated
Carry an identification card stating you take disulfiram, the reaction symptoms, and a contact for emergencies
Report immediately any fatigue, weakness, nausea, vomiting, jaundice or dark urine (possible liver injury)
This drug is an aid, not a cure - continue supportive and psychotherapeutic treatment
pk: Slow GI absorption; full effect on alcohol sensitivity develops over the first hours to days
Sensitivity increases with continued therapy (no tolerance develops)
Alcohol reaction possible up to 14 days after the last dose
Store at 20-25 C; dispense in a tight, light-resistant container
pearls: Never give to an intoxicated patient or without the patient's full knowledge
Patient must abstain from alcohol at least 12 hours before the first dose
Avoid alcohol in all disguised forms; reactions can occur up to 14 days after stopping
Contraindicated with metronidazole, paraldehyde, severe myocardial disease, coronary occlusion and psychoses

missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is nearly time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your usual schedule; do not take two doses at once. Do not stop the drug or drink alcohol to compensate.
overdose: No specific information is available on the treatment of disulfiram overdose. Contact the local Poison Control Center and provide supportive care.
